morgan: Heads-up — intermittent mkdocs build failure on main CI. Seems related to anchor resolution when headings include trailing emojis or inline HTML blocks. Failing job: https://circleci.com/gh/redwood/docs/12345 ashley: Can you paste the snippet + the exact error from the logs? I can take a look. morgan: Yep. File: docs/guides/deploy.md. Repro pattern: a heading like `## Quick start 🚀` followed immediately by an HTML table and then a code block. CI log shows: ``` ERROR: Could not resolve fragment 'quick-start' in page 'deploy.md' File ".../site/deploy.html", line 1, in mkdocs.exceptions.ConfigurationError: Fragment 'quick-start' referenced but no matching anchor found ``` sam: I ran into something similar last quarter when a heading ended with a colon (`## Options:`). Different markdown/slugify libs treated punctuation differently, so slugs changed across environments. yu: Two practical options: 1) Make anchors explicit where they matter: `## Quick start {#quick-start}` (requires attr_list / markdown extensions). 2) Normalize headings during CI/docs-lint (strip emojis/punctuation) or inject explicit fallback anchors in build step. Also consider pinning the slugify/markdown extension versions in pyproject/requirements to avoid behavior drift. ashley: Attr_list isn't enabled in our mkdocs.yml right now — flipping that could have side effects. Normalizing headings in a linter seems less risky. Could we run a quick transform script that flags ambiguous headings and suggests `{#...}`? morgan: I'll prototype a tiny script that scans for headings with trailing punctuation/emojis and either adds an explicit `{#id}` or emits a lint error. Example heuristic: lowercase, replace spaces with `-`, remove punctuation. sam: For the CI flake, also check for HTML blocks right after headings — that seems to trip the parser sometimes. A pre-commit regex that warns on `^#{1,6} .*\n<\w` (heading followed by an HTML tag) would catch a lot. ashley: Good call. Can you paste the offending markdown slice? morgan: Sure: ```markdown ## Quick start 🚀
Example
```bash echo "deploy" ``` This pattern reliably produced the CI error in Circle logs. yu: Another low-risk mitigation: detect unresolved fragment errors in the build step and convert them into a warning for one run while we patch docs, so PR cycles don't get blocked by legacy headings. Then flip back to failing after cleanup. morgan: Opening a small PR with two pieces: (A) a docs-lint script to flag ambiguous headings and (B) a tiny CI tweak to pin mkdocs-mdx/slugify behavior for now. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4567 ci-bot: Build retriggered for morgan/patch-quickstart — CircleCI job 67890 queued :white_check_mark: ashley: :100: Thanks. Please include a short note in the PR description explaining the heuristic and the reason for pinning. Also add a test case in docs-lint that includes an emoji/colon heading to avoid regressions. sam: I'll add the pre-commit hook for the heading+HTML detection. Simple Python regex and a unit test should do. morgan: PR opened and linked above, added changelog + tests. Tagging @ashley @yu for review, low-risk Markdown-only change. Thx :pray:
